title: Context Economy Strata Skim — takeaways and micro-actions
content:
Quick personal skim of several conference talks / papers + blog links — focused on the interplay between context window economics, KV cache strategies, and practical latency/cost levers. This is intentionally terse; capture memetic ideas and micro-actions I can take this week.

1) High-level thesis I keep returning to:
- Not all tokens are equal: distribution of useful tokens is heavy-headed (recent prefixes matter most for many tasks). Therefore cache + routing + model variant strategies can buy disproportionate cost/latency wins.
- The trick is bridging offline eval (perplexity/regression) with online SLOs (p99 latency, tail cost, quality queries).

2) Papers / talks skimmed (notes + immediate impression):
- "Adaptive Prefix Sampling for Long Contexts" (conf talk) — idea: dynamically decide prefix retention by attention footprint instead of fixed eviction.
  - Impression: plausible low-hanging fruit for our serving runtime; add as feature flag experiment: sample retention window by token salience.

- "KV-Shard Rebalancing under Workload Skew" (paper) — smart shard reassign to reduce hot-spot tails.
  - Note: maps to Dedicated mode pain points where tenant burst hits a subset of shards. Add to backlog: simulation harness in infra to model tenant burst patterns (start with synthetic Zipf).

- "Quantization-aware Cache Fidelity" (short poster) — low-bit kernels change attention noise; cache admission needs to be quantization-aware.
  - Implication: when offering quantized model variants in the same rollout, tag cache entries by quantization profile to avoid cross-variant contamination.

- Blog: "Latency SLOs vs. Unit Cost: a practical guide" — pragmatic batching heuristics (dynamic batch cap tied to p99 latency budget).
  - Action: prototype dynamic-batch-cap policy in the canary runtime (config param + perf telemetry).

3) Concrete experiments to sketch this sprint (priority order):
- E1: Prefix-salience eviction test (low effort)
  - Instrument: compute token salience proxy (top-k attention mass per token) in a lightweight offline pass on representative prompts (RAG + long instructions from support logs).
  - Metric: token retention rate vs. model quality (ROUGE/QA accuracy) and cost per response.
  - Outcome target: >=15% token saved with <2% quality delta.

- E2: KV-shard hotspot simulator + greedy reassign policy
  - Build: simple event-driven simulator (tenant arrival, KV read/write heat) — reuse parts of capacity-sim code in infra/plate.
  - Metric: p99 latency under 3 burst profiles; compare baseline and greedy-reassign.

- E3: Cache tags for quantized variants (medium effort)
  - Implement: tag cache keys with model-quant-id; measure hit rate drop and false positive contamination.
  - Risk: cache index memory overhead + slight increase in miss rate; measure delta.

4) Quick heuristics and mental models I want to remember:
- If you can recover 10–20% of recently repeated tokens via prefix caching you often get >20% token-cost reduction because batching/throughput effects compound.
- Tail latency is often dominated by cache-miss amplification: a miss triggers longer model path + KV recompute + backend RPCs. Reducing miss variance pays p99 dividends.
- Model variants (float16->int8) reduce per-token cost but increase subtle quality noise — don’t mix variants in a shared cache without guarding keys.

5) Unresolved questions (for follow-up):
- What’s the right lightweight salience metric that our runtime can compute cheaply? Top-1 attention mass? Token gradient proxy?
- How much added index overhead will per-variant cache tags add for large-scale caches (10B entries)? Estimate memory delta with a 2-byte variant id vs. absolute bytes.
- Where to expose these knobs in console? Per-model boolean flags (salience-eviction, quant-tagging, shard-policy) or automatic suggestions from Optimize?

6) Notes-to-self / next steps (this week):
- Draft a 1-pager for eng-sre + serving-runtime: elevator description + proposed E1 experiment + required infra telemetry (p50/p90/p99 by route, cache-hit tagged by model-id). (Due: Fri)
- Open a sandbox PR: add minimal cache-key tag plumbing (feature-flagged). Link to INF-2034. (Start: Tue)
- Sync with Asha on simulator idea; try to reuse her arrival traces from last quarter. (Ping Slack #kv-cache: "hotspot-sim sync?")

7) Useful links clipped here for later reading: (save full texts to confluence later)
- "Adaptive Prefix Sampling" — slides: https://conf2026.org/papers/adaptive-prefix.pdf
- "KV-Shard Rebalancing" — arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12345
- Blog: Latency SLOs vs Unit Cost: https://engineering.blog/llm-latency-costs

8) One-paragraph summary I can paste into a sprint update:
- Investigated a set of recent papers on context-cost tradeoffs. Priorities: (1) a cheap prefix-salience eviction experiment to reclaim tokens while preserving quality, (2) a KV-shard hotspot simulator to explore reassign policies for tail mitigation, and (3) cache tagging for quantized model variants to prevent cross-variant pollution. I’ll produce an eng 1-pager and a sandbox PR this week to kick off E1/E3.

——

summary: Personal quick-skim of context-economy talks/papers; shortlist of three experiments (prefix-salience eviction, KV-shard simulator, cache-tagging for quantized variants) + next steps and links.
